met_analysis:
The Western Disturbance as a cyclonic circulation over north Punjab & neighbourhood between 3.1 & 4.5 km above mean sea level persists. However, the associated trough aloft in middle & upper tropospheric westerlies with its axis at 5.8 km above mean sea level roughly along Long. 72°E to the north of Lat. 30°N has moved away East-Northeastwards.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over south Haryana & neighbourhood now lies over South Haryana & adjoining north Rajasthan and extends upto 1.5 km above mean sea level.
An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over South Rajasthan & adjoining north Gujarat at 0.9 km above mean sea level.
An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over South Coastal Andhra Pradesh & neighbourhood between 0.9 & 4.5 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over southeast Arabian Sea & adjoining Lakshadweep persists and now seen at 0.9 km above mean sea level.
The trough from upper air cyclonic circulation over southeast Arabian Sea & adjoining Lakshadweep to northwest Arabian Sea at 0.9 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over south coastal Tamil Nadu extending upto 1.5 km above mean sea levelhas become less marked.
The trough from upper air cyclonic circulation over south coastal Tamil Nadu to Northwest Bay of Bengal off Odisha coast across Southwest & Westcentral Bay of Bengal extending upto 1.5 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
The trough from northeast Uttar Pradesh to Eastcentral Arabian sea across East Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra at 3.1 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
